plan.subject: LLM agents

queries.query: ("LLM agent" OR "language model agent" OR "LLM-based agent" OR "agentic LLM")
queries.rationale: Catches papers that explicitly frame themselves around LLM agents using the most common naming variants.

queries.query: ("autonomous agent" OR "autonomous LLM agent" OR "autonomous language agent") AND ("large language model" OR LLM OR "language model")
queries.rationale: Finds agent work described through autonomy language rather than the exact phrase LLM agent.

queries.query: ("agent workflow" OR "agentic workflow" OR "multi-step reasoning" OR "tool-using agent") AND (LLM OR "large language model" OR "language model")
queries.rationale: Targets engineering-relevant workflow and execution patterns that change how agents are structured in practice.

queries.query: ("multi-agent" OR "multi-agent system" OR "society of agents" OR "agent collaboration") AND (LLM OR "large language model" OR "language model")
queries.rationale: Covers coordination, role assignment, and collaboration architectures beyond single-agent designs.

queries.query: ("tool use" OR "tool-augmented" OR "function calling" OR "API calling") AND (LLM OR "language model" OR agent)
queries.rationale: Surfaces papers on one of the most practically important capability shifts for real-world agents: calling tools and external APIs.

queries.query: ("planning" OR "task decomposition" OR "hierarchical planning" OR "plan-and-execute") AND ("LLM agent" OR "language model agent" OR "LLM")
queries.rationale: Captures architectures that improve agent behavior through explicit planning, decomposition, and staged execution.

queries.query: (memory OR "long-term memory" OR "episodic memory" OR "retrieval memory") AND ("LLM agent" OR "language model agent" OR agent)
queries.rationale: Finds work on persistent state, contextual recall, and memory systems that materially affect agent capability over longer horizons.

queries.query: (reflection OR "self-reflection" OR "self-critique" OR "verbal reinforcement") AND ("LLM agent" OR "language model agent" OR LLM)
queries.rationale: Targets iterative refinement methods where agents critique and improve their own outputs or plans.

queries.query: ("retrieval-augmented generation" OR RAG OR retrieval) AND ("LLM agent" OR "agentic system" OR "language model agent")
queries.rationale: Catches work where agent behavior is changed by integrating retrieval and external knowledge access.

queries.query: ("code agent" OR "software engineering agent" OR "coding agent" OR "programming agent") AND (LLM OR "language model")
queries.rationale: Emphasizes the engineering-heavy agent literature most likely to matter to a software engineer building practical systems.

queries.query: (benchmark OR evaluation OR "agent benchmark" OR AgentBench OR SWE-bench OR GAIA) AND ("LLM agent" OR "language model agent" OR agentic)
queries.rationale: Finds papers that define how agent performance is measured, including benchmark papers and evaluation methodology.

queries.query: (hallucination OR reliability OR robustness OR safety) AND ("LLM agent" OR "language model agent" OR "autonomous agent")
queries.rationale: Surfaces limitations and failure analyses relevant to deploying agents that actually work in practice.

queries.query: ("web agent" OR "browser agent" OR "GUI agent" OR "computer-using agent") AND (LLM OR "language model")
queries.rationale: Covers agents that operate websites, interfaces, and desktop-like environments, a major practical application frontier.

queries.query: ("embodied agent" OR robotics OR robot) AND ("large language model" OR LLM OR "language model agent")
queries.rationale: Brings in adjacent but important work where agent architectures are tested in grounded, action-taking environments.

queries.query: ("agent tuning" OR finetuning OR alignment OR preference) AND ("LLM agent" OR "language model agent" OR "agentic system")
queries.rationale: Targets methods for adapting or training models specifically to improve downstream agent behavior.

plan.coverage_notes: This plan covers core agent terminology, major architectural levers like planning, memory, tool use, reflection, and multi-agent coordination, plus practical angles such as coding agents, web agents, evaluation, and reliability. It deliberately avoids overly product-specific framework queries and very broad standalone terms like agent or workflow that would drift off-topic. The profile assumption driving the plan is that this reader wants research that changes implementation choices for real systems, so the queries lean toward architectural patterns, benchmarks, and deployment-relevant failure modes.
